player.speaker: Revolutionary Delegate
line.artelt-cold-open.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-cold-open.text: Keep that order open. Let every stoker see the Admiralty seal. Berlin is asking for an armistice, and the admirals still mean to spend us in one last battle with Britain. They call it honour. Below decks we call it choosing our own grave.
line.artelt-opening.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-opening.text: Thüringen and Helgoland showed them the fleet would not sail. The admirals broke up the squadrons; on the canal back to Kiel, they seized forty-seven men—most from Markgraf. I have the prison list here. Two hundred and fifty sailors met at the Union House for them last night; Souchon still would not receive the delegation.
line.garbe-union-house.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-union-house.text: Nor will he receive another. The police have chained the doors of the Union House. Five hundred sailors are gathering outside; the meeting has moved to the Großer Exerzierplatz, and the presses are running for tomorrow. The words passing through the yards are peace and bread.
line.popp-socialists.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-socialists.text: Good. A locked door has done what our petitions could not: every shipyard now knows this is larger than forty-seven arrests. Give me the station and telegraph, and by dawn Souchon will face a citywide movement—not an isolated mutiny he can bury.
line.artelt-confronts-popp.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-confronts-popp.text: Call it larger if that makes the printers work faster. Those forty-seven are the reason the crews trusted us. Leave them behind while we seize a switchboard, and every stoker in Kiel learns that a movement values its message more than its men.
line.garbe-steinhaeuser.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-steinhaeuser.text: Another runner from Feldstraße. Lieutenant Steinhäuser has formed thirty recruits across the road to the prison. Rifles loaded. He says the march stops there.
line.popp-coordination.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-coordination.text: The men at the hall chose you to coordinate the armed columns because Karl must hold the torpedo crews and I must bring out the yards. That gives you men, Delegate—not time. We can force the service gate before Steinhäuser closes it, or secure the station, telegraph and armouries before Souchon cuts Kiel off. Which moves first?
line.popp-coordination.choice.free-priso: The prison. Take a small party through the service gate now; the main column follows before Steinhäuser can turn the road into a firing line.
Gain an experienced half-strength sailor detachment and +50 prestige; the remaining escapees appear exposed inside the compound and must be reached before the guards break them up.
line.popp-coordination.choice.secure-com: Coordinate the city first. Put runners on the station, telegraph and armouries, then hold the rescue column ready for the prison.
Gain +140 prestige and +15 experience for every core formation; no prisoners appear at setup, but approaching the compound starts the rescue crisis and gives you one turn to break through.
line.popp-prisoners-objection.speaker: Lothar Popp
line.popp-prisoners-objection.text: Then I will keep the presses moving with whoever is left. But if Souchon cuts the wires, we may free one prison and leave every barracks in Kiel believing his version of tonight.
line.garbe-prisoners.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-prisoners.text: The service gate is open—the first men are out and asking for rifles. The rest are caught in the inner yard; the alarm is hammering through the base. Steinhäuser's men are turning towards them. Reach the compound before the guards break the escape apart.
line.artelt-communications-objection.tex: Then my rescue column waits—but it does not vanish into somebody's timetable. The moment those runners return, we march on Feldstraße. If the guards fire, remember whose minutes we spent.
line.garbe-communications.speaker: Gustav Garbe
line.garbe-communications.text: Orders are moving through the yards. The columns will muster by district, with rifles accounted for and every section knowing its road. The forty-seven remain behind Souchon's wall. When your rescue column nears the compound, the crowd will move with it—and Steinhäuser will open fire.
line.souchon-warning.speaker: Governor Souchon's Headquarters
line.souchon-warning.text: Order from Naval Governor Souchon: the Union House is closed. Disperse all unauthorised assemblies. Lieutenant Steinhäuser's patrol will block the march to the Feldstraße detention compound. Loyal detachments are to secure the station, telegraph and military depots. Ringleaders will be arrested before the morning watch.
line.artelt-final.speaker: Karl Artelt
line.artelt-final.text: There's his answer. No petitions, no delegation—only loaded rifles between us and our comrades. Sailors, soldiers and workers move together. Disarm those who resist, take in those who join, and keep the ships in harbour. No one sails to die for an empire that has already lost its war.
